Hi Alicia — great speaking with you and John. Following up with the items from your InfoSec checklist: see attached subprocessor list (redwood_subprocessors_v3.csv) and our redacted SOC 2 Type II (redwood_soc2_type2_redacted.pdf).

Quick notes on the subprocessor list:
- Primary compute/data: AWS (us-west-2) for hosted API; GCP (us-east1) used for batch embedding jobs for a small subset of customers who requested it.
- Vector DB / embeddings cache: We use an optional managed vector store partner (VectorFlow) which is listed as an output-only processor — we do not send raw PII to them by default; only hashed or tokenized embeddings per customer config.
- Monitoring/logging: Datadog (ingestion: service metrics + structured traces). Logs containing customer input are redacted by default; raw request/response artifacts are only retained per customer retention policy and are accessible via a secure portal for debug with customer consent.
- Auth / Secrets: AWS KMS + HashiCorp Vault (keys under customer-managed KMS if requested for Private deployments).

GDPR/HIPAA: Redwood supports regional data jurisdictions and offers a Private deployment option and contractual clauses (DPA, SCCs) for GDPR. For HIPAA: our platform can be configured for HIPAA-eligible deployments (BAA available for Dedicated/Private customers).

Next steps I propose:
1) I'll upload the attachments here and share a short summary doc.
2) Laura (security lead) will join a 30-min call with your team to walk the SOC 2 scope and subprocessor controls — can you share 2 windows this week?
3) If your team prefers, we can start the Acme questionnaire in parallel; we've got a security questionnaire owner who can intake and track the items.

Thanks — attaching the files now.

Hi Acme team — Laura from Redwood Security here. Thanks for the review. Answers below inline: 

1) VectorFlow: we have a data flow diagram and an architecture note. For most customers embeddings are one-way hashed/tokenized before being sent; there is a \"no-forwarding\" config we can enable for Acme so embeddings never leave the primary cluster. I'll attach the flow diagram and a short architecture note in our next message.

2) Subprocessors outside US/EU: we engage a small number of contractors for model tuning and labeling in APAC; those contractors do not receive plaintext production traffic. Any human-assisted review is performed on redacted or consented data under strict NDA and access controls. Cross-border transfers are covered by SCCs/DPAs where applicable.

3) SOC 2 scope: The Type II covers our hosted API, authentication, logging, and vendor management processes for the period 2026-01-01 to 2026-12-31. The redacted report covers the controls tested; the full report can be shared under NDA if required.

POC for questionnaire: Markus Klein (markus@redwood.ai) will own the intake and return SLA. Typical SLA for the first pass is 5-7 business days for standard Acme templates; shorter if we can prioritize.
